title: Health entropy mitigation and tiered shedder for SLO protection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Production services are experiencing autoscaler instability during transient multi-region incidents caused by noisy health signals and short-lived capacity pressure. This ticket scopes a mitigation that reduces 'health entropy' (flapping/readiness noise), introduces a tiered shedding policy (soft per-token admission then hard shutdown), and ties shedding decisions to SLO-preserving regional failover rules. Goal is to prevent wide-scale thrash while preserving P95/P99 latency SLOs for customer traffic.

Background: Several incidents in Q1 showed oscillation where instances flip ready/unready in under 30s due to transient GPU memory pressure and backend retries. Autoscaler reacts to aggregated health leading to scale-in/scale-out cycles and increased latency. Current health pipeline reports raw liveness/readiness booleans without temporal smoothing or token-weighting for request importance.

Scope: Design and implement a mitigation path that: (1) smooths readiness signals using an entropy-aware sliding window metric, (2) implements a tiered shedder which first rejects non-interactive/batch tokens and eventually applies strict admission to preserve hard SLOs, (3) provides regional damping rules that prevent autoscaler handoff during brief noise spikes, and (4) adds a simulation harness to validate behavior under synthetic failure modes. Not included: full-blown admission-controller rewrite and UI work for Console (follow-up ticket will own Console visibility).
proposed_solution:
1) Health entropy metric: compute a moving-window entropy score per instance and per region (e.g., scaled Shannon entropy of recent readiness samples + variance of latency). Expose this as a health_score used by autoscaler rather than raw boolean.
2) Tiered shedder: implement two thresholds: soft_shed (apply to low-priority token classes, e.g., embeddings/background jobs) and hard_shed (apply to all except pinned high-priority tokens). Soft_shed returns 429 with Retry-After and optional cached response; hard_shed triggers circuit breaker for the instance and redirects traffic to regional fallback.
3) Token-weighted admission: incorporate request contract (customer SLA tier, token cost estimate) into admission decisions so high-value requests are prioritized during constrained capacity.
4) Autoscaler damping: add hysteresis windows and a minimum stabilization period when health_score fluctuates, and prevent immediate failover to other regions unless sustained degradation > configured window.
5) Simulation harness & metrics: extend our chaos simulator to inject short memory pressure spikes, packet delays, and request fanouts to validate no autoscaler thrash and SLO preservation.

Implementation notes: keep changes behind a runtime feature flag for staged rollout. Provide observability: health_score timeseries, shed counts by token class, regional handoff logs.
acceptance_criteria: New health_score produced and consumed by autoscaler in canary cluster
Under simulated 30-90s memory pressure spikes, autoscaler should not perform scale-in/out more than once per 10 minutes
P95 latency degradation <= 10% and P99 <= 20% for high-priority tokens during synthetic failure scenarios
Soft_shed rejects non-critical tokens with documented Retry-After and increments shed metrics
Regional failover only occurs if health_score remains below hard_shed threshold for > configured window
Runbook updated with playbook for tuning thresholds and rolling back feature flag
tasks: Implement tiered shedder in admission layer (backend team)
Add token-contract tagging to request pipeline (SDK/edge)
Integrate health_score into autoscaler decision path (scaling team)
Extend chaos simulator and run test matrix (SRE)
Documentation: runbook, config knobs, Console summary (PM/Docs)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync — aligned on entropy metric and tiered shedding approach. Diego to prototype entropy window. PM requested explicit guardrails for customer traffic.
2026-03-04: Prototype shows entropy metric reduces false positives on canary by ~40% in replayed traces. Observability prototype pushed: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/health/entropy-canary
2026-03-06: Design review with scaling team — agreed minimum 5m stabilization window; agreed to expose soft_shed ratio per customer tier. Action: create schema for token-contract tags.
2026-03-08: PR opened for sliding-window health_score: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021 — needs tests and review from @maria-nguyen

2026-03-10: Simulation harness extended to inject memory pressure patterns; initial run shows autoscaler thrash eliminated in 8/10 scenarios. Remaining work: edge SDK tagging and production canary rollout plan.
decisions: Use a combined entropy + variance health_score instead of simple rate-based smoothing to capture both flapping and jitter
Adopt a two-tier shedding model (soft -> hard) to maximize request preservation while protecting SLOs
Enforce a default 5 minute autoscaler stabilization window; make configurable per deployment profile
Feature flag rollout starting in us-west-2 canary cluster, then gradual expansion to multi-region once metrics meet thresholds
risks: Incorrect health_score tuning could mask real failures and delay necessary autoscaler action
Token-weighted admission may prioritize high-revenue customers disproportionately — needs fairness review
Soft_shed behavior might increase client-side retry storms if Retry-After semantics are ignored
Regional damping could delay legitimate multi-region failover during long outages if thresholds too lenient
qa_plan: Stage 1: unit & integration tests for health_score math and shedder. Stage 2: run chaos sim suite against canary cluster. Stage 3: 48h canary with synthetic traffic replay of last incident. Monitor P95/P99 and shed metrics. Abort if P99 for high-priority tokens increases >20%.
rollback_plan: Toggle off feature flag to restore previous admission logic. If autoscaler state divergence observed, scale to safe capacity via manual override and follow runbook to reconcile instance readiness states. Post-rollback: run diagnostic to capture snapshot of health signals for tuning.
